findings.problem: FindPeakDirect still materializes RMS-weighted pixels before scanning, duplicating functionality already provided by SimpleWeighted.
findings.concrete_cost: Every weighted call writes a full scratch image and then scans it. At 4096×4096, the scratch write alone is 64 MiB, followed by scratch reads. This occurs in scale-zero searches, squared-channel searches, and the nonoptimized minor loop.
findings.proposal: Reuse SimpleWeighted at work/radler/cpp/math/peak_finder.cc:190, passing the existing borders and selected mask. Preserve per-scale mask precedence, float-rounded products, signed values, first ties, sentinels, and the subsequent normalization division. Retain materialization for unmasked AVX searches because their public semantics differ; the existing dispatch at work/radler/cpp/algorithms/threaded_deconvolution_tools.cc:194-203 demonstrates that boundary.
findings.history: Blame traces materialization to the older RMS path; commit 1f1452ea introduced the reusable fused scan in the threaded caller.

findings.problem: ConvolvePsfs and RunComponentOptimization repeatedly forward-transform the same PSF for different scales despite an existing API for reusing its FFT.
findings.concrete_cost: For K transformed scales, each loop performs K forward image FFTs where one suffices: K−1 redundant two-dimensional FFTs per PSF.
findings.proposal: Compute the PSF spectrum once per invocation with schaapcommon::math::ConvolutionFft, then reuse MultiScaleTransforms::Transform(const std::complex<float>*, Image&, float) at work/radler/cpp/algorithms/multiscale/multiscale_transforms.cc:143-147. The existing caller at work/radler/cpp/algorithms/threaded_deconvolution_tools.cc:91-95,148 demonstrates this reuse. Preserve destination ownership, logical transform dimensions, tail bytes, and each loop's current scale-zero behavior.
findings.history: Blame places these loops before b053bedc, which introduced the pretransformed overload specifically to avoid repeated image FFTs.

findings.problem: The owning-image transform passes its disposable FFT workspace through the const-spectrum convolution API, which allocates a second spectrum. An existing internal helper already supports consuming the first buffer.
findings.concrete_cost: ConvolveTransformed allocates and frees another spectrum per image: approximately 64 MiB of additional live storage at 4096×4096. Its initialization copies the original spectrum while multiplying.
findings.proposal: Follow-up only: expose a consuming convolution overload backed by MultiplyAndInverse at work/schaapcommon/src/math/convolution.cc:131-150, using the existing nullptr image_fft mode demonstrated at lines 160-161. Consume only the local image_fft workspace. Preserve the const API for shared spectra, immutable published kernels, exact multiplication order, inverse hooks, logical prefixes, and the documented in-place exception contract.
findings.history: Blame attributes both consuming and copying modes to 6ae8c4c; the separate const-input route deliberately supports spectrum reuse.

findings.problem: RunComponentOptimization allocates an image-sized scratch buffer used exclusively as an ignored Transform argument.
findings.cost: One unnecessary 4*width*height-byte heap allocation per image optimization call: 64 MiB at 4096².
findings.proposal: Default-construct scratch instead. Keep the existing Transform interface and ownership/exception behavior.

findings.problem: ConvolvePsfs duplicates the same nonzero-scale transform across both branches and copies the zero-scale PSF again at line 71, although the initial copy remains unchanged.
findings.cost: An unnecessary full-image copy for each integrated zero-scale entry: 64 MiB copied at 4096², plus duplicated control flow.
findings.proposal: Perform the guarded nonzero-scale transform immediately after the initial copy. Retain the integrated metadata/logging branch and remove its redundant zero-scale assignment.
findings.history: Blame and e15a38e1 show both variations were carried through the ASP helper extraction.

findings.problem: FindPeakDirect still materializes RMS-weighted pixels and duplicates masked dispatch despite the existing SimpleWeighted utility.

findings.proposal: Follow-up optimization: select the effective mask once and use SimpleWeighted for weighted masked searches and non-AVX unmasked searches. Preserve the existing unmasked AVX fallback, binary32 products, signed peaks, first ties, sentinels, and normalization division. Verify through independent caller-level oracles before adopting; speedup needs measurement.
findings.history: Blame traces materialization to the original implementation; 1f1452ea added this optimization only to the threaded caller and explicitly preserved AVX behavior.

cleanup-quality.json.summary: Reviewed the complete bundle and scoped live callers, utilities, and history. Two safe simplifications and one CPU optimization follow-up. Costs are static estimates. No edits, builds, tests, or benchmarks performed.

findings.problem: FindWithMask now inherits a full scalar rescan of every improving row, continuing after the already-computed row maximum has been found. Blame traces this behavior to the weighted implementation in 1f1452e; this diff newly extends it to unweighted masked scans.
findings.concrete_cost: With an all-true mask and increasing row maxima in the first column, the new path visits every pixel twice. Stopping position recovery at that first maximum would reduce second-pass visits from width*height to height.
findings.proposal: For the new unweighted specialization, locate the first allowed pixel equal to row_peak, record its coordinates, and stop scanning that row. Retain the outer strict-improvement guard and signed return value, preserving ties, NaNs, infinities and sentinels. Keep the independent test oracle unchanged.
